key_insight: Ferroelectricity in CaBi2B2O9 (B = Ta, Nb) comes from coupled polar and octahedral distortion modes, with interlayer sliding between Bi2O2 layers and perovskite blocks acting as the fundamental structural driver.
engineering_relevance: This identifies a design rule for layered oxide ferroelectrics: tune stacking-induced interlayer displacement to enhance polarization, piezoelectricity, and insulating behavior for high-temperature devices.
method: Group-theoretic symmetry analysis of the ferroelectric phase transition
First-principles calculations of polarization, piezoelectric response, and energetics
Mode decomposition of Γ5−, X2+, and X3− distortion coupling
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a consistent theoretical picture from symmetry analysis and first-principles results showing that trilinear mode coupling deepens the ferroelectric well and explains the intrinsic insulation and polarization trends.
watch_item: The conclusions are computational and materials-specific, so experimental confirmation of the proposed interlayer-sliding mechanism and its robustness under defects, strain, or processing conditions is still needed.
paper_title: The origin of ferroelectricity, polarization and high resistivity in Aurivillius CaBi2B2O9 (B = Ta, Nb)
